slides.title: Where we are
items: A servomotor rotates to the angle we command and holds it there. Inside it are a DC motor, a gear train, a potentiometer on the output shaft, and a control circuit with an H-bridge.
The command is a pulse on its signal lead, and the width of the pulse determines the position.
The servo is powered from the regulator board's 5V pin, never from the Nucleo, and only the signal lead goes to a pin capable of PWM. We'll use PA7 (D11).
What you need today: Nucleo and breadboard, AD2, potentiometer. No servo yet.
Today we'll design the timer that creates that pulse and then check the pulse on the AD2 oscilloscope. We'll wire the servo tomorrow.
